title: Care Billing Allowance on Long-Term Hardship Hold Recertifications
content:
**Medical client bulletin — Hardship and Protective Holds.** When an updated physician's medical or disability certification is asked for on a running Long-Term Hardship Hold, a care billing allowance is added once to the days allowed for the recertification. It depends on the consumer's medical debts placed with Ridgeline, as shown by the consumer's Placed Consumer Accounts records (debt type and status), because a medical bill placed so recently that it is still in its validation period points to treatment that is still being billed and a physician who is harder to reach.

| The consumer's placed medical accounts | Care billing allowance |
|---|---|
| At least one is still in its validation period (status validation period) | 5 calendar days (recent-care allowance) |
| There are placed medical accounts, but none is still in its validation period | 2 calendar days (older-care allowance) |
| No placed medical account | None |

**Points of reading.**

- All of the consumer's placed medical accounts count, not only the held account.
- One medical account in its validation period is enough for 5 days, however many other medical accounts the consumer has.

**Example (hypothetical).** The consumer's held account is a bank card debt; the consumer also owes two placed hospital bills, one active and one arranged. There are placed medical accounts, none in its validation period: 2 calendar days are added.
